external_entities.name: customer
external_entities.description: A person who browses and places sock orders through the mobile app.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application customers use to browse and order socks; it talks to the web API.
processes.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: web API
processes.description: The API used by the mobile app; it keeps customer data, hands orders to SIMS, and receives catalogue updates from spreadsheet macros.
processes.source_excerpt: The app talks to the web API over HTTP — not HTTPS
processes.notes: Nobody here can tell me what the API does about authentication

processes.name: SIMS
processes.description: The stock and inventory system that receives orders, writes delivery addresses to a flat file, and sends dispatch notes to the fax gateway.
processes.source_excerpt: SIMS does two things with an order.
processes.notes: It has been running since long before the app existed.

processes.name: spreadsheet macros
processes.description: Macros in the marketing spreadsheet that send SQL statements to the web API to change prices and product copy.
processes.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy
processes.notes: The spreadsheet is described as a stopgap that is still in use.

data_stores.name: user database
data_stores.description: The database where the web API keeps customer names, addresses, and the cards they paid with.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the user database ... [is] encrypted.

data_stores.name: flat file
data_stores.description: A flat file kept alongside SIMS containing delivery addresses only.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file kept alongside it — only addresses go in that file, nothing else
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the ... flat file [is] encrypted.

data_stores.name: spreadsheet
data_stores.description: The marketing spreadsheet containing the product catalogue, including prices and product copy.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet.
data_stores.notes: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

data_flows.name: browse and order
data_flows.description: Customer browsing and ordering through the API via the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app
data_flows.notes: The customer acts through the mobile app; the flow is represented to the component that answers.

data_flows.name: talks to API
data_flows.description: The mobile app communicates with the web API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app talks to the web API over HTTP — not HTTPS

data_flows.name: keep customer data
data_flows.description: The web API stores customer names, addresses, and payment card data in the user database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database
data_flows.data_description: Customer name, address, and payment card data

data_flows.name: hand over order
data_flows.description: The web API hands an order to SIMS.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When an order is placed the API hands the order over to SIMS

data_flows.name: write delivery address
data_flows.description: SIMS writes the delivery address to the flat file.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file

data_flows.name: send dispatch note
data_flows.description: SIMS sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway

data_flows.name: fax confirmation
data_flows.description: The fax gateway faxes the customer a confirmation containing their name and address.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which faxes the customer a confirmation with their name and address on it
data_flows.notes: The gateway dials the number stored against the order and nobody checks it arrived at the right place.
data_flows.data_description: Confirmation with customer name and address

data_flows.name: read catalogue
data_flows.description: The spreadsheet macros use the catalogue in the spreadsheet.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API
data_flows.notes: The source describes the macros as being in the spreadsheet.

data_flows.name: change catalogue
data_flows.description: The spreadsheet macros send SQL statements to the web API to change prices and product copy.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy

trust_boundaries.name: office
trust_boundaries.description: The office location where the marketing laptop hosting the spreadsheet is located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.
trust_boundaries.notes: This is the only explicitly described location or zone.

assumptions.assumption: The web API is internet-facing because customers use the online service through the mobile app.
assumptions.basis: The description says Sokify sells socks online and that customers browse and order through the mobile app, which talks to the web API.

assumptions.assumption: The user database is confidential because it contains customer names, addresses, and payment card data.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the database contains customer name, address, and the card they paid with.

assumptions.assumption: The flat file is confidential because it contains delivery addresses.
assumptions.basis: The source states that only delivery addresses are stored in the flat file.

assumptions.assumption: The office is a network trust boundary because it is an explicitly named organizational location.
assumptions.basis: The spreadsheet is stated to live on a marketing laptop in the office.
